Governance: Ohio Department of Natural Resources, Division of Forestry (primary); Division of Parks and Watercraft (portion through State Park)
Description: Ohio's signature state forest backpack trail, traversing 40+ miles of rugged ridges and hollows through the Shawnee wilderness. The main loop offers a shorter 23-mile North Loop and a 17-mile South Loop option. Blazed orange throughout. The trail overlaps with the Buckeye Trail (yellow blaze) and the North Country National Scenic Trail (blue blaze) for portions of the route. Passes through approximately 8,000 acres of designated wilderness within Shawnee State Forest. Multiple backcountry campsites.
Identity Notes: Primary parent: Shawnee State Forest (SC-S-0004 pending). Secondary parent: Shawnee State Park (SC-S-0005 pending) — trail traverses park boundary. Orange blaze throughout; overlaps Buckeye Trail (yellow) and North Country Trail (NCT, blue). North Loop (~23 mi) and South Loop (~17 mi) are route options within the 40+ mi main circuit, not separately named trails — do not create separate Trail entities for loops. Multi-county: spans Scioto and Adams counties. Trail is the most significant recreational trail in Scioto County. Shawnee Bridle Trail Network (SC-TN-0001 pending) is a separate equestrian system on different routes.
